hypotheses.name: IRGC captured the succession (weak form — assessed finding)
hypotheses.d: Documented pressure on Assembly electors, 8 boycotts, overridden shortlist and will. The pre-arranged-pact version scores only 30% — the plan was overridden, not executed.

hypotheses.name: The IRGC, not Mojtaba, rules Iran (working model) — HELD 82%
hypotheses.d: HELD. The promised authenticated footage of Mojtaba meeting commanders still has not landed, so the falsifier remains un-run. The week was IRGC-forward — the Guard, not the foreign ministry, confirmed it ran the Oman channel and announced the revenue-sharing terms, and the Guard made the mine-strike claim — but that is DENIED as a raise under the shared-prediction rule: 'the Guard runs the maritime file' is predicted just as strongly by an ordinary reading in which the IRGC is a powerful institution under a functioning Supreme Leader, which is a much weaker claim than 'the IRGC rules Iran'. The 82% cap stands for exactly the reason it was set.

hypotheses.name: The Iran file is coalition-captured (the capture read, tracked as opinion)
hypotheses.d: The claim: on the Iran file, organized coalition pressure — donor networks, primary structure, allied commitments, defense-institutional momentum — outweighs the base's war fatigue, which is why a 'no more wars' White House struck anyway and now substitutes sanctions for settlement rather than sign a visible retreat before the midterms. Mechanisms named, plural: status clock vs electoral clock, sunk cost after declaring victory, lobbies as veto players that raise the price of defection (one interest group among several — any single-key version of this hypothesis is scored separately and currently rejected). Held at 70%: the strike itself, the 6-month grind, and 'not in a hurry' all fit; capped because the same facts also fit ordinary planning failure plus vanity. Falsifier: a signed de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz reopening BEFORE the midterms — the base's clock winning on the party's most captured file would kill the strong form outright.

hypotheses.name: Nobody's hurrying on Hormuz — 60% → 65% (RAISED)
hypotheses.d: Its first fact that BEATS a rival instead of merely fitting itself. On 30 Aug the US struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak after observing Guard personnel preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait — two days after CENTCOM declared the lanes fully cleared, and while Muscat negotiates a minesweeping calendar. The 08-30 audit had installed a genuine rival — a physical clock, minesweeping simply takes time — and ruled this hypothesis must beat it. A physical clock runs down; this one is being rewound, by the exact actor the hypothesis named in advance. Capped at +5 on three counts kept in front: CENTCOM is the interested party and 'observed preparations' is unpublished intelligence used to justify a strike; Al Jazeera published a technical challenge on 31 Aug to whether Iran can even mine by rocket as claimed; and IRGC counter-coercion against a blockade that has redirected 83 vessels, disabled three and boarded two explains the same act without any rent motive. Not pre-event.

hypotheses.name: Détente as harvest cover — HELD 60%, tell sharpened
hypotheses.d: August continues the signature: 125 PLA aerial ADIZ incursions (the 2026 decline intact) against 152 non-warship PRC vessels in the first 21 days, ~60% coast guard, with the east-of-Taiwan patrols now a declared 'new normal'. Kinetic down, jurisdiction up. NOT moved — this is the same signal that bought +5 on 08-26, and re-marking on the continuation of its own evidence is the double-count the audit named. The important item is against my own test: if Beijing has DECLARED the patrols permanent, their persistence through the Sept 24 visit is close to uninformative. Re-specified now, in advance and stricter — the informative observation on 09-23→09-25 is a boarding, an inspection, or a first-time-area incursion. Mere presence no longer counts as confirmation.

hypotheses.name: Venezuela was a Hormuz hedge in a drug-war uniform
hypotheses.d: The clearest revealed-preference play on the board — and the reason it holds at 55 rather than higher. Sturdy mechanism first: US Gulf-Coast refineries are plumbed for heavy sour crude, Venezuela sits on the planet's largest heavy reserves, and moving that barrel north through the Caribbean to Texas and Louisiana structurally hedges the one risk that ran live all year — a Hormuz closure. The Aug 28-29 deal (a new operator taking control of ~65bn barrels, about a fifth of Venezuela's reserves) is exactly what this hypothesis predicts. So oil-as-motive is near-certain. What is NOT settled — and what caps this — is premeditation: was Southern Spear a counter-narcotics and regime-change campaign that harvested the oil after the fact, or an oil-security operation in a drug-war uniform from the start? The tell against design is the clock — the deal trailed Maduro's Jan 3 capture by eight months, which reads more like spoils than master plan. Falsifiers: token export volumes, Gulf-Coast heavy sourcing not actually swinging off the Middle East, or the fixed infrastructure (GEO-022) never appearing. One correction the excitement needs: a canal cannot bypass Hormuz — the hedge is source substitution plus Caribbean routing, not a waterway. Note it is DISTINCT from 'The Portfolio State' below, which is about the vehicle rather than the motive.

hypotheses.name: US drift hardened into leverage play — HELD 52%
hypotheses.d: Confirming but shared, therefore ambience: Treasury again held back on Chinese financial institutions, with mainstream reporting now naming the mechanism outright — designating them 'could create tensions before Xi's visit'. Bessent's promised weekly cadence hit banks but no Chinese one, and at the G20 he pushed severing Iran financial ties while China dissented. Both the leverage read and the ordinary 'Washington won't detonate its own summit' read predict all of it. The strongest weekly argument AGAINST, logged rather than absorbed: the US struck Iran on three consecutive nights and took Iranian fire onto three Arab host states. Deliberate slow-walking for leverage sits badly with sustained kinetic escalation that raises the cost of the thing being slow-walked — that counterweight is what holds the number at 52.

hypotheses.name: A pre-announcement leak into oil futures — 40% → 34% (biggest mover)
hypotheses.d: Its lead conditional has now gone unfired across three weeks containing the most violently market-moving Iran news since April — the 30 Aug Larak strike, three nights of exchanges, two struck VLCCs, Brent to ~$95 — with not one reported nine-figure pre-announcement episode. The file is confirmed as historical and bounded: DOJ is probing four trades totalling ~$2.6bn, all inside a five-week window that closed in April — Mar 23 (>$500m, ~15 min before Trump's delay post), Apr 7 ($960m before the ceasefire), Apr 17 ($760m, ~20 min before Iran said Hormuz was open), Apr 21 ($430m before the extension). CORRECTION BANKED AGAINST THIS ENTRY: the ledger's earlier '~$2.2bn cluster' for Mar 23 and its '~$7bn' aggregate are both withdrawn as over-wide constructions. The cut is made on the hypothesis's own written terms, not on a preferred reading — a conditional set at 60% has burned three of fourteen weeks in the best environment it will ever get and produced nothing. The cut is only −6 because of one genuinely new structural fact: investigators are running a SEPARATE probe into prediction-market activity on the same developments, and the same foreknowledge reaching two unrelated venues is hard to explain as one market-maker hedging client flow. Split now: deliberate leak 34 / mediator-side 20 / skilled opportunism 36 / coincidence 10. Still the only entry whose evidence is timestamped BEFORE the event.

hypotheses.name: NEW · The Portfolio State — coercion converted into sovereign equity, statute retrofitted
hypotheses.d: Strongest form: the US is converting military and sanctions leverage into permanent state equity in strategic supply chains, with the legal authority written to fit transactions rather than the reverse — Venezuela being the first hydrocarbon use of a template already run in chips and critical minerals. The rail predates the headline, which is the only thing licensing a design read at all: Senate NDAA FY2027 §1051 was marked up in MID-JUNE — ten weeks before the 29 Aug deal — creating a DoD Equity Investment Account, authorising OSC equity to $500m and capping any single position at 40% of the entity; the Venezuela stake is 35%, inside a cap that does not legally exist yet. Add DoD's own $400m/15% stake in MP Materials with 100% offtake (structurally identical to Venezuela's '20% of output at cost'), House Oversight already demanding an accounting of Venezuelan oil revenue on 23 Feb, and CFR's tally of 26 government equity deals worth ~$23.9bn. It opens at only 25% because the boring, incompetence and patronage readings are all strong: think tanks have been publicly naming and counting this pattern since 2025 (a policy, not a plot); the Pentagon's own spokesman flatly DENIES that OSC takes equity while WSJ reports it doing so, which is improvisation not design; and a 100-year concession over 65bn bbl routed to one politically connected operator with no published contract is better explained as spoils allocation. Above all the base rate is enormous — Anglo-Persian 1914, the RFC, GM/Chrysler 2009 — so the design premium must be small. NOT a conspiracy claim and must never be scored as one: it requires no secrecy at all, only anticipation, and the honest gap is that I cannot name the operator who executes the warrants. Key test: does the ENACTED NDAA widen §1051 beyond critical minerals to energy, or raise the cap, by 31 Dec (45%)? Scope enacted unchanged kills the design read.

hypotheses.name: Moscow shapes Tehran's maximalism — 25% → 22% (CUT, sixth session running)
hypotheses.d: The week finally produced Russia-Iran material and it is the wrong KIND. Moscow said publicly on 01 Sep that air defence is the main focus of military-technical cooperation with Iran, alongside a reported 500 Verba MANPADS and 2,500 missiles and continued fighter deliveries. That is the resupply leg — already priced at 7/10 under 'means'. It moves nothing: it is announced by TASS, an interested party publishing its own helpfulness and the structural opposite of a covert channel; the opportunism branch predicts arms sales to a client at war identically, so under the standing rule it is ambience; and after six sessions there is still ZERO documentary evidence Moscow has influenced Tehran's negotiating position, which is the actual claim. Arms transfers are not persuasion. Cut rather than held because a decay rule that bites only on its deadline is a cliff, not decay. Clock unchanged: 15% on 30 Sep absent documentary evidence, retire below 10%.

hypotheses.name: War pause was secretly packaged with the Beijing summit — on the retirement line
hypotheses.d: Nothing resolved this week, and one file addition cuts against it: the summit's Iran content is now openly reported as an explicit US ask — Chinese pressure on Tehran to reopen the strait — with Beijing expected to want Taiwan concessions in return. An openly negotiated Iran-for-Taiwan trade is this hypothesis's RIVAL, not its confirmation; the secret-package version needs the deal hidden, and the deal is being conducted in headlines. Retirement trigger unchanged; the test runs on schedule on 24 Sept.

brief.head: DR Congo pledges to move its embassy to Jerusalem
brief.h: Felix Tshisekedi reaffirmed the relocation after a visit to Israel and meetings with Benjamin Netanyahu and Isaac Herzog, joining a short list of states that have promised the move since Washington made it in 2018.
brief.t: Recognition is the one currency a poor state can print. Kinshasa has little leverage over anybody, but it has a flag, a vote and an embassy address, and all three are transferable. What it wants is not Israeli - it is American pressure on Rwanda over the armed advances in the east, which is the single external variable that decides whether Tshisekedi governs his own mineral belt. So read this as a payment, not a conviction: the cheapest available offering to the party that actually controls the file, routed through a third capital because that is the route Washington has priced.
brief.context: The rail predates this presidency. Since the 2018 US move, the practice has been to trade recognition for a security or economic good - Guatemala, Honduras, Paraguay, Papua New Guinea, Fiji and now a fresh Colombian announcement all sit on that ledger, and Tshisekedi first made this pledge at the UN General Assembly in September 2023 without acting on it. The deciding desk is not the Congolese foreign ministry but the State Department office running the Rwanda-DRC track alongside the minerals-for-security arrangement. The base rate is the part to hold onto: pledges to move embassies to Jerusalem outnumber completed moves by a wide margin, and several states that announced under the 2018 wave never opened a chancery. What would change the read is a budget line and a building.

angles.effect: Gains a hearing in Washington on the Rwanda file at near-zero fiscal cost, and a visible foreign-policy win while the east is losing
Gains an African signature at a moment when its diplomatic column is short, and the precedent that the price of recognition is still payable
Pays - each pledge, even an unexecuted one, erodes the convention that final status decides the capital
Pay the chancery cost, if it is ever built, for a benefit that accrues to one negotiating track

dec.kill: A published relocation date, budget appropriation or named chancery site. Absent those within six months, this stays a UNGA-season pledge of the kind that has repeatedly expired.

brief.head: US investigators point to an American munition in Iran wedding strike
brief.h: Military investigators believe the blast that killed at least four people at a wedding in Kuhestak on Tuesday night was a direct hit by a US weapon - on the day the Vice President called Iranian accounts of it doubtful and said he would not call the conflict a war.
brief.t: Two claims collided in one afternoon. Reuters reported that US military investigators assess the Kuhestak deaths came from an American munition, while JD Vance told the White House briefing room he was extremely sceptical because Iranian state media has not been a very good scribe about the conflict - and the President had already said flatly that Iran did it, because their munitions have no accuracy. Set the atrocity question aside for a moment and look at the second sentence Vance offered, which is the load-bearing one: he said he would not call this a war, that there is no active shooting, and that major combat operations ended after about six weeks. That is not commentary. That is the legal posture on which the absence of a War Powers clock, a casualty-compensation regime and a congressional vote all rest.
brief.context: The rail is Operation Epic Fury, which the Pentagon declared over on 5 May, and everything since has been run as residual defensive activity rather than a named campaign. That classification is what lets an air war in its seventh month proceed without the sixty-day reporting clock the War Powers Resolution attaches to hostilities - which is why the naming fight matters more than it sounds. The deciding desk is CENTCOM's civilian-harm assessment cell plus the defence department's general counsel, not the podium. Base rate, and it is unflattering: US civilian-casualty investigations historically confirm a minority of allegations and take months to publish, with findings often arriving after the political moment has closed. What would change the read is a CENTCOM assessment naming a US weapon, or a member of Congress forcing a privileged War Powers vote that makes the terminology justiciable.

angles.effect: Gains time and legal room - no war means no clock, no vote, and no formal compensation obligation, while the investigation absorbs the news cycle
Gains the strongest atrocity claim of the campaign, and it is now reportedly corroborated by the adversary's own investigators rather than only by state television
Pay - they absorbed Iranian fire this week from bases whose sorties they must now defend domestically against a civilian-casualty story
Pays by default, its war power eroded one classification at a time rather than by any single vote it lost

dec.kill: A published CENTCOM civilian-harm assessment attributing the Kuhestak deaths to Iranian ordnance, with munition fragments or flight-track evidence. That would vindicate the President's version and turn the Reuters report into a sourcing failure.

consp.claim: That the wedding blast was Iranian ordnance falling short and is being laundered into an American atrocity - the mirror claim, running alongside it on the same threads, is that the US did it knowingly and the investigation exists to bury it past the news cycle. Both circulate under a broader claim that the stated duration of this war has been a deliberate lie from the start.
consp.spread: The Persia Israel General on /pol/ at over 300 replies, whose own header mocks the timeline - day 187 of the four-day special military operation to regime change Iran - alongside a running Ukraine-war equivalent.
consp.read: Two incompatible false-flag readings held simultaneously, which is the signature of a board treating all official statements as noise rather than choosing between them. The checkable kernel is real and unusual: the President and the Vice President blamed Iran and doubted the report while their own investigators reportedly concluded the opposite, and that gap is on the record. The duration mockery is the more durable frame and the better-founded one - a campaign declared finished in May is still killing people in September.

brief.head: Volkswagen approves 50,000 more job cuts, taking the total to 100,000
brief.h: The supervisory board signed off Oliver Blume's overhaul: roughly 50,000 further posts on top of 50,000 already agreed, about 15 per cent of global staff, with the long-term futures of the Hannover, Emden, Zwickau and Neckarsulm plants no longer guaranteed.
brief.t: This is the largest restructuring in the history of the car industry, larger than the 50,000 General Motors shed through its 2009 bankruptcy, and it is being done by a solvent company in peacetime. That is the tell. Volkswagen is not resizing for a recession, it is resizing for a world where it does not win China and no longer has cheap Russian gas - the two assumptions its entire cost base was built on. The plan buys that with 135 billion euros of investment to 2031, a target of 9 per cent operating margin on about 9 million vehicles by 2030, and a model line cut by as much as half by 2035. Fewer cars, made by fewer people, sold at higher margin - the strategy of a firm that has conceded volume.
brief.context: The rail is co-determination. Lower Saxony holds about 20 per cent with a blocking stake and IG Metall sits on the supervisory board, which is why this arrives as attrition, early retirement and alternative uses for plants rather than as closures - the German industrial settlement does not permit the American verb. Watch that euphemism, because it is where the real decision hides: a plant converted to defence or battery work is a different story from a plant wound down, and the board has committed to neither. The deciding desks are the works council and the Lower Saxony state chancellery, not Wolfsburg alone. Base rate: announced auto restructurings deliver roughly the headcount they promise and miss the margin target, because the margin depends on a product cycle nobody controls. This is also the same squeeze as two other cards on this board - Chinese competition on the output side, an energy shock on the input side.

angles.effect: Gains its clearest mandate yet, and a number large enough to reset expectations before the next cycle judges it

angles.party: IG Metall and the works council
angles.effect: Gain the form of the process - voluntary terms, no forced redundancies - while losing the substance, four plants without guarantees
Pay, and Lower Saxony and Saxony pay first, in a tax base that does not have a replacement employer
Gain the volume Volkswagen is voluntarily vacating, in the segments the model cull removes

dec.kill: Named alternative uses with committed capital for Hannover, Emden, Zwickau and Neckarsulm. Conversion with a funded buyer would make this a restructuring; silence past the works council vote would make it a staged withdrawal.

consp.claim: That the cuts prove a foreign power deliberately hollowed out European industry, and separately that they destroy the case for free-market capitalism outright - an ethnic and national scapegoat framing of the China trade is circulating around the announcement, using a slur-led shorthand that assigns intent to a whole population rather than to a firm or a policy.
consp.spread: A /pol/ thread reading the cuts as a warning to Canada, at around 100 replies, and a shorter thread arguing the announcement kills what faith was left in free markets.
consp.read: The scapegoat move here is the standard substitution of a people for a policy, and naming the technique is the point: the checkable kernel - Chinese EV competition plus a permanent European energy cost step-up - is a real and sufficient explanation that requires no intent at all. It is downstream of the 2024 plant-closure scare, which ended in a negotiated settlement, and that memory is why the board reads this announcement as confirmation rather than news.

brief.head: US diesel hits a record $5.82 a gallon as the middle barrel breaks
brief.h: The national average reached $5.820, edging past the June 2022 peak, with East Coast distillate stocks at a record-low 19.3 million barrels and the diesel crack spread touching an all-time $108 a barrel.
brief.t: This is not a crude story, and the numbers say so. Brent is around $97, high but not historic, while the refining margin on diesel is at an all-time record - which means the shortage is in the middle of the barrel, not in the ground. Two cuts caused it and both are physical: roughly 900,000 barrels a day of diesel and 350,000 of jet fuel used to move through the Gulf, about ten and twenty per cent of global seaborne supply, and Ukraine's drone campaign has damaged enough Russian refining that Moscow banned its own diesel exports through 30 September. Distillate is the fuel that moves freight, runs farms and heats houses, so it is the one product whose price walks straight into food and rent with a lag of a month or two.
brief.context: The rail is inventory, and it was thin before this shock started. August distillate stocks were the lowest for the month since 1982 and the East Coast number is the lowest since the series began in 1990 - the buffer that normally absorbs a chokepoint closure was already gone. The deciding desk is not the White House but the refiners themselves, and they are already running at multi-year utilisation rates to capture a record crack, which is the honest answer to any pressure campaign: there is no idle capacity left to lean on, and jawboning does not create hydrotreating units. Base rate: cracks this wide normally mean-revert within two quarters, but only when either refining capacity returns or crude quality improves, and neither is scheduled. Northern-hemisphere harvest and southern-hemisphere planting both raise demand from here, before heating season even starts.

angles.effect: Gain the best margin environment on record - the record crack is the counterpart of the record pump price, and it is booked as earnings
Pay directly and first, and cannot substitute - there is no consumer response to a diesel price on the way to a harvest
Pays politically for a price it has attributed to Ukraine's refinery strikes, while its own Hormuz posture is the larger physical cause
Gains scarcity value on the barrels it can still export, having been forced to stop exporting diesel to protect its own domestic supply

dec.kill: Two consecutive EIA weeklies showing East Coast distillate builds while the crack narrows below $60. That would mean the supply cut is being routed around rather than absorbed, and the record was a spike rather than a level.

consp.claim: That the true state of American energy costs is being managed and hidden - a thread posting the all-time-high diesel print sarcastically as proof that the promised golden age has arrived as a price shock, and that the reopening talk is cover for a permanent step up in the cost of living.
consp.spread: A fresh /pol/ thread built around the diesel record, running beside a grocery-price thread and a longer one arguing conditions are worse than in any poster's lifetime.
consp.read: The managed-numbers frame in its cheapest form, but the checkable kernel is now confirmed rather than alleged: the record is real, EIA-sourced and on the wire, and the diesel crack has been the standout stress in this shock for weeks. What the frame adds is intent - it needs the number to be concealed, and this one was published.

brief.head: Norway seizes a Russian ship at Svalbard over Ukraine's $4.2bn award
brief.h: A Norwegian court ordered the arrest of the research vessel Professor Molchanov on 31 August, and the coast guard took it at Barentsburg after a standoff, on behalf of Naftogaz's unpaid Hague award for assets expropriated in Crimea.
brief.t: The vessel is a 43-year-old oceanographic ship running tourist cruises and is worth almost nothing against a $4.22 billion judgment. That mismatch is the story: this is not debt collection, it is the arbitral-enforcement rail arriving in the Arctic. Naftogaz won at The Hague in 2023 for property Russia took when it annexed Crimea, and it is now running enforcement in roughly ten jurisdictions, with Russian assets already attached in Finland and France. What makes Norway different is the venue. Barentsburg is a Russian company town on a Norwegian archipelago, and the Svalbard Treaty of 1920 gives Moscow a treaty right to be there - so an attachment executed at that specific quay tests the one place where Russian presence on NATO territory is legally guaranteed.
brief.context: The rail is ordinary commercial attachment law, not sanctions, and that distinction is the whole point - sanctions freeze, attachment transfers. Courts pierce sovereign immunity only for assets in commercial use, which is why a cruise-carrying research hull is a better target than a state icebreaker, and why the ship's operating profile rather than its flag will decide the appeal. The deciding desk is a Norwegian enforcement court and the coast guard that executed for it, with the foreign ministry conspicuously not in the frame. Moscow has called it piracy and Arctic minister Alexei Chekunkov called it legal nihilism, which is the response you give when the instrument is legal and you would rather argue about legitimacy. Base rate: most attachment attempts against Russian state-linked assets have been released on immunity grounds within months, so the burden is on this one to survive appeal. What would change the read is a second NATO state attaching a hull under the same award.

angles.effect: Gain proof of concept - an award that was paper for three years produced a physical seizure, which raises the value of the other enforcement tracks
Gains nothing it wanted and carries the risk, having let a commercial court do what its foreign ministry would not have chosen at Barentsburg of all places
Pays a trivial asset and gains a grievance with treaty texture - the Svalbard framing is the most usable thing Moscow has been handed in the Arctic this year
Pays in insurance and port risk, because any commercially operated hull in a signatory jurisdiction is now a candidate

dec.kill: A Norwegian appellate court releasing the vessel on sovereign-immunity grounds. That would confine this to a first-instance ruling rather than an enforcement rail, and would stop the copycat filings it otherwise invites.

consp.claim: That the seizure is a rehearsal for confiscating the roughly $300 billion of frozen Russian central bank reserves - that Western governments are laundering expropriation through private arbitration awards so the taking looks like a court order rather than a policy, and that the Arctic was chosen because nobody will fight over a tourist ship.
consp.spread: The two standing Ukraine-war generals on /pol/ at roughly 180 and 140 replies, plus a thread asking directly how Russia and Europe can de-escalate without one of them collapsing.
consp.read: The confiscation-by-proxy frame. The kernel is checkable and partly right: enforcement of the Naftogaz award is genuinely running in about ten jurisdictions, and the reserves debate is real and live in Brussels. Where it fails is the mechanism - an arbitral award against Russia is a private creditor's judgment, and the immunity doctrine that protects central bank reserves is precisely the doctrine this ship's owner will invoke on appeal. The two questions run in opposite legal directions.

watch: Whether CENTCOM publishes a civilian-harm assessment on Kuhestak naming the munition, and whether any member of Congress files a privileged War Powers resolution against the not-a-war framing. The classification, not the casualty count, is what has been load-bearing for seven months

Whether the next two EIA weeklies show East Coast distillate building from 19.3 million barrels, and whether Moscow extends its diesel export ban past 30 September. Refiners are already at multi-year run rates, so there is no domestic lever left to pull

Whether a Norwegian appellate court releases the Professor Molchanov on sovereign-immunity grounds, and whether a second NATO state attaches a Russian hull under the same Naftogaz award. One seizure is a ruling; two is an enforcement rail

Whether Volkswagen names funded alternative uses for Hannover, Emden, Zwickau and Neckarsulm before the works council signs. A converted plant and a wound-down plant are the same press release and completely different outcomes

Whether Kuwait or the UAE publicly restricts US offensive sorties from their soil after taking fire this week. Host tolerance, not Iranian capability, remains the binding constraint on the air campaign
